cues.en: So I designed tools and, this is what some of them look like.
cues.zh: 所以我设计了一些工具，其中一些是这样的。

cues.en: So these are tools for people making software, making electronics,
cues.zh: 这些是给做软件、做电子、

cues.en: making music, animation, working with mathematical equations.
cues.zh: 做音乐、动画、处理数学方程的人用的工具。

cues.en: These areas where you're making something that that does stuff. So you're making something that has complex behavior. And my focus has always been on
cues.zh: 这些领域里，你造的东西是有功能的。你造的东西有复杂的行为。而我一直关注的是

cues.en: how can the creator see that behavior? How can they see what the thing they're building is actually doing?
cues.zh: 创作者怎么看到那个行为？他们怎么看到自己正在构建的东西实际在做什么？

cues.en: And what are powerful ways of seeing so they can understand
cues.zh: 有哪些强大的观察方式，让他们能理解

cues.en: what that thing is doing?
cues.zh: 那东西在做什么？

cues.en: Now these have generally been software based tools.
cues.zh: 这些工具一般都是基于软件的。

cues.en: And what software based means today
cues.zh: 而今天所谓基于软件

cues.en: is that these tools are trapped inside a tiny rectangle that sits on your desk. And do your work, you sit at your desk and you stare at this tiny little rectangle.
cues.zh: 就是这些工具被困在你桌上一个小小矩形里。你要干活，就坐在桌前盯着这个小矩形。

cues.en: And that frustrates me. Because if you think about
cues.zh: 这让我很沮丧。因为你想，

cues.en: a lot of the traditional forms of craftsmanship, they take place in a spatial environment, a room that's designed for that purpose,
cues.zh: 很多传统的手工艺都发生在空间环境里，一个为此专门设计的房间，

cues.en: where the worker is surrounded by tools,
cues.zh: 工匠被工具环绕，

cues.en: where they can walk around, use their body, use their hands, think spatially.
cues.zh: 可以走动，用身体、用手，进行空间思考。

cues.en: The room itself kind of becomes a macro tool they're embedded inside. It's like an extension of their body.
cues.zh: 房间本身就成了他们身处其中的宏观工具，像是他们身体的延伸。

cues.en: So I've been taken with this idea of designing tools in the form of rooms,
cues.zh: 所以我一直着迷于把工具设计成房间的形式，

cues.en: in the form of spatial environments.
cues.zh: 设计成空间环境的形式。

cues.en: And so I was thinking about this and thinking about space for making things, and that led to thinking a little bit about
cues.zh: 于是我琢磨这件事，琢磨创造事物的空间，这就引出了

cues.en: makerspaces.
cues.zh: 创客空间。

cues.en: So makerspaces are these communal workshops that are becoming popular nowadays where people come together to create in a shared social environment,
cues.zh: 创客空间是如今越来越流行的公共工作坊，人们聚在一起，在共享的社交环境中进行创造，

cues.en: and they have access to
cues.zh: 并且他们能够使用

cues.en: powerful high end equipment that they wouldn't be able to afford as individuals.
cues.zh: 个人无力负担的强大高端设备。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: I really like these two aspects of makerspace. I like
cues.zh: 我非常喜欢创客空间的这两个方面。我喜欢

cues.en: creating in a shared environment. I like access to powerful tools. And I like the
cues.zh: 在共享环境中创造。我喜欢使用强大的工具。我还喜欢

cues.en: philosophical motivations
cues.zh: 这一理念动机

cues.en: behind this maker movement that instead of, consuming mass produced products, people should make their own things.
cues.zh: 也就是创客运动背后的理念：人们不应消费批量生产的产品，而应自己动手制作。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: so what I wanted to share with you today was this idea for how to take these maker goals
cues.zh: 今天我想和大家分享的想法，是如何把这些创客目标

cues.en: to the next level. So what I'd like to do is I'd like to design a new kind of space
cues.zh: 提升到新层次。我想做的是设计一种新型空间，

cues.en: that enables and empowers creators in ways that today's maker spaces don't really support.
cues.zh: 以当今创客空间未能真正支持的方式，赋能并支持创作者。

cues.en: So if you go into a maker space today,
cues.zh: 如果你现在走进一个创客空间，

cues.en: you'll probably see a laser cutter
cues.zh: 你大概会看到激光切割机

cues.en: and you might see a three d printer
cues.zh: 可能还会看到3D打印机

cues.en: and welding equipment
cues.zh: 以及焊接设备

cues.en: and plastic forming equipment and lathes and mills and drills
cues.zh: 塑料成型设备、车床、铣床和钻床

cues.en: and sawing and sewing and soldering. And these are all wonderful tools,
cues.zh: 还有锯切、缝纫和焊接工具。这些都是很棒的工具，

cues.en: but these are all construction tools. These are all tools for taking material
cues.zh: 但这些都是建造工具。这些都是把材料

cues.en: and sticking it together. Right? And
cues.zh: 拼接在一起的工具。对吧？而且

cues.en: those are precisely the tools you need if you're making something like furniture
cues.zh: 如果你在做家具之类的东西，

cues.en: or if you're making simple mechanical contraptions.
cues.zh: 或者做简单的机械装置，这些正是你需要的工具。

cues.en: But more and more, we're seeing people making a different kind of project. More and more people are making things like robots that roll around,
cues.zh: 但越来越多的人在做不同类型的项目。越来越多的人在制作能四处滚动的机器人、

cues.en: robots that fly around, robots you can talk to, that tend your garden,
cues.zh: 能飞行的机器人、能与你对话的机器人、能照料花园的机器人、

cues.en: clothing that lights up, clothing that responds to how you move or responds to people around you,
cues.zh: 会发光的衣服、能响应你的动作或周围人的衣服、

cues.en: musical instruments,
cues.zh: 乐器、

cues.en: bike displays,
cues.zh: 自行车显示屏、

cues.en: machines that scan books,
cues.zh: 扫描书籍的机器、

cues.en: three d printers,
cues.zh: 3D打印机、

cues.en: self balancing vehicles.
cues.zh: 自平衡车。

cues.en: So all of these kinds of projects have a high amount of internal complexity,
cues.zh: 所有这些项目都有很高的内部复杂度，

cues.en: often with embedded software,
cues.zh: 通常还涉及嵌入式软件，

cues.en: and that give rise to complex
cues.zh: 这会产生复杂的

cues.en: behavior.
cues.zh: 行为。

cues.en: They're often taking an input from the outside world and then responding to that world
cues.zh: 它们通常从外部世界接收输入，然后以复杂的方式

cues.en: in complex ways.
cues.zh: 对这个外部世界做出响应。

cues.en: And when you're making a project of this sort,
cues.zh: 当你做这类项目时，

cues.en: the primary challenge is not putting the pieces together. The primary challenge is understanding
cues.zh: 主要的挑战不在于把各个部分拼起来。主要挑战在于理解

cues.en: what the thing is doing and why it's doing that and how you can get it to do what you actually want it to do. So for example, if you're making a little robot and that robot's supposed to move towards the light, you put down your robot and you turn on the light and it does not move towards the light. What
cues.zh: 这个东西在做什么、为什么那样做，以及如何让它做你真正想让它做的事。比如，如果你在做一个小机器人，它本该朝光移动，你把它放下、打开灯，它却不朝光移动。你

cues.en: do you do?
cues.zh: 会怎么做？

cues.en: Well, you have to get in there. You have to get inside that robot's head and see what it's seeing and see what it's thinking and come to understand
cues.zh: 你得深入进去。你得钻进那个机器人的脑子里，看它看到了什么、在想什么，进而弄明白

cues.en: why it's behaving the way it's behaving. And the construction tools aren't gonna help you here. What you need here are seeing tools
cues.zh: 它为什么会有这样的行为。构建工具在这里帮不上忙。你需要的是观测工具，

cues.en: And we don't really have many of those.
cues.zh: 而我们实际上并没有多少这样的工具。

cues.en: And the few seeing tools that we have tend to be very primitive tiny rectangles that sit on your desk.
cues.zh: 我们已有的少数观测工具，往往是非常原始的、放在桌上的小方块。

cues.en: On the other hand, there are a few people out there that take seeing really seriously.
cues.zh: 另一方面，有一些人非常认真地对待“观测”这件事。

cues.en: So for example,
cues.zh: 比如，

cues.en: here's how NASA does it. So if you're launching a space shuttle, you need to understand everything that's going on in this very complex system. So they have sensors everywhere
cues.zh: NASA 是这么做的。如果你要发射一架航天飞机，你需要理解这个非常复杂的系统里发生的一切。所以他们在各处都装了传感器，

cues.en: and they designed this room, this spatial environment,
cues.zh: 还设计了这个房间，这个空间环境，

cues.en: where you can sit there and you can see and understand
cues.zh: 让你可以坐在那里，看到、理解

cues.en: and control every last little bit of that system.
cues.zh: 并控制那个系统的每一个细节。

cues.en: This is Fermilab, control room at Fermilab, the particle accelerator in Illinois.
cues.zh: 这里是费米实验室，伊利诺伊州粒子加速器的控制室。

cues.en: This is the California power grid
cues.zh: 这是加州电网

cues.en: and this is a Canadian power grid.
cues.zh: 这是加拿大电网。

cues.en: This is a waste treatment facility.
cues.zh: 这是废物处理设施。

cues.en: This is a TV station.
cues.zh: 这是电视台。

cues.en: And this is the Large Hadron Collider at CERD where they recently found the Higgs boson. These people know that if you're trying to design a system of this complexity,
cues.zh: 这是欧洲核子研究中心的大型强子对撞机，他们最近在那里发现了希格斯玻色子。这些人明白，如果要设计如此复杂的系统，

cues.en: that you have to understand in real time,
cues.zh: 就必须实时理解，

cues.en: you have to build a room. You have to build a room where you can go in there and understand that everything that's going on.
cues.zh: 必须建一个房间。建一个能走进去、理解一切正在发生什么的房间。

cues.en: And that's the kind of thinking that I'd like to bring to mainstream engineering
cues.zh: 我想把这种思维方式带到主流工程

cues.en: and making.
cues.zh: 和制造中。

cues.en: What I'd like to do is take this idea of a maker space and transition it to the seeing space.
cues.zh: 我想做的是把创客空间这个理念转变到观察空间。

cues.en: Create a environment
cues.zh: 创造一个环境

cues.en: that's entirely around seeing and understanding what the project that you're building is actually doing.
cues.zh: 完全围绕观察和理解你正在构建的项目实际在做什么。

cues.en: Shifting the focus from putting the pieces together to deep understanding. So it's almost like a a giant microscope that you're embedded inside
cues.zh: 把焦点从拼装零件转向深度理解。就像一台你身处其中的巨型显微镜

cues.en: that's focused on what you're building.
cues.zh: 聚焦于你正在构建的东西。

cues.en: Now when I think about a a seeing space like this, I think on... I think about seeing on three different levels.
cues.zh: 当我想到这样的观察空间时，我想到……我想到在三个不同层面上的观察。

cues.en: Three progressively more powerful
cues.zh: 三种逐步更强大的

cues.en: ways of seeing. The first step
cues.zh: 观察方式。第一步

cues.en: before you can see anything is you need something to see.
cues.zh: 在你看到任何东西之前，你需要有东西可看。

cues.en: So you need a way of collecting data and a way of displaying that data.
cues.zh: 所以你需要一种收集数据的方式和一种展示数据的方式。

cues.en: So you make this little robot.
cues.zh: 你做出这个小机器人。

cues.en: The way many of these projects are done today is with a kind of last century stinginess where you put on just the bare minimum sensors and the bare minimum processing power, the bare minimum communication capabilities.
cues.zh: 如今很多这类项目的做法，还带着上世纪的吝啬劲儿——只装最基本的传感器、最基本的处理能力、最基本的通信能力。

cues.en: And so as a result, most of the information you'd actually want to see is never collected or accessible
cues.zh: 结果就是，你真正想看到的大部分信息，根本就没被采集到，也无法访问

cues.en: in the first place.
cues.zh: 从一开始就是这样。

cues.en: I've seen so many projects
cues.zh: 我见过太多项目

cues.en: fail at some point because some wire came loose.
cues.zh: 在某个时刻失败，就因为某根线松了。

cues.en: And the conventional thinking is, oh, that's the fault of the builder for not attaching the wire strongly enough. The way I see it is it's the fault of the wire for being too dumb to know whether it's attached. Right?
cues.zh: 而传统思维是，哦，那是制作者的错，线没接牢。但在我看来，那是线的错——它太笨了，不知道自己有没有接上。对吧？

cues.en: We now live in a world where sensing... Sensors are cheap, processing is cheap. We need to start working with smarter materials
cues.zh: 我们现在所处的世界，传感……传感器很便宜，处理很便宜。我们得开始用更智能的材料

cues.en: that collect a lot of data about what's going on out there, collect a lot of data about what's happening inside the box, and then can transmit that data up into the room.
cues.zh: 去采集大量关于外部情况的数据，采集大量关于盒子里内部情况的数据，然后把这些数据传到房间里。

cues.en: And then we design the room in such a way that reflects all that information
cues.zh: 然后我们把房间设计成能把所有这些信息

cues.en: back to the maker.
cues.zh: 反馈给制作者。

cues.en: And so you can put information on walls,
cues.zh: 所以你可以把信息放到墙上，

cues.en: You can project onto the workbench. There's many ways of displaying information.
cues.zh: 可以投影到工作台上。展示信息的方式有很多。

cues.en: The point is you have to get that stuff out of the box and into the environment where anything that you would want to know is just kind of a glance away.
cues.zh: 关键在于，你得把这些东西从盒子里弄出来，放进环境里，这样任何你想知道的事，抬眼一看就都有了。

cues.en: And then once you have the means of collecting data and the means of displaying data, now you can start to think about
cues.zh: 然后，一旦你有了收集数据的手段和显示数据的手段，你就可以开始思考

cues.en: how should we display that data? What are powerful ways of representing this kind of information?
cues.zh: 我们该如何显示这些数据？有哪些强大的方式来表示这类信息？

cues.en: And one of the most powerful ways is time.
cues.zh: 其中最强大的方式之一就是时间。

cues.en: So we tend to think moment to moment, see things moment to moment. And it's not until you step back from those moments and look across a range of time at once that you can start to see patterns,
cues.zh: 我们往往是一刻接一刻地思考，一刻接一刻地看事物。只有当你从那些瞬间中抽身出来，同时纵观一段时间，你才能开始看到模式，

cues.en: that you can start to think about systemic causes.
cues.zh: 才能开始思考系统性的原因。

cues.en: So if you have your little robot and you let it go
cues.zh: 所以如果你有你的小机器人，你把它放出去

cues.en: and it did something weird back there, just like a few seconds ago, it did something.
cues.zh: 它在那边做了些奇怪的事，就像几秒前，它做了点什么。

cues.en: That moment went past, but what did it do back there? Right? You wanna be able to grab it and run it back.
cues.zh: 那一刻过去了，但它在那边到底做了什么？对吧？你希望能抓住它、把它倒回去。

cues.en: And why not? You know, why not work in a space where there's video cameras everywhere, everything's being recorded, everything's being marked and tracked. You just look up and bring it up, grab time,
cues.zh: 为什么不呢？你知道，为什么不在一个到处都是摄像头、一切都被记录下来、一切都被标记和追踪的空间里工作呢？你只要抬头一看，把它调出来，抓住时间，

cues.en: run it back, see what happened. Right? Take time and put it into the maker's hands.
cues.zh: 倒回去，看看发生了什么。对吧？把时间交到创客手中。

cues.en: And then think about ways of seeing across time.
cues.zh: 然后想想跨越时间的观察方式。

cues.en: So look at the path that the robot followed, Look at all the data that was collected during that run. Be able to browse through it. See what was going on with the external sensors. See what was happening inside the box. Take measurements on that data.
cues.zh: 看看机器人走过的路径，看看那次运行期间收集的所有数据。能够浏览这些数据。看看外部传感器的情况。看看盒子内部发生了什么。对这些数据进行测量。

cues.en: Compare
cues.zh: 比较一下

cues.en: what happened this time to what happened last time. Understand the effects that your changes are having.
cues.zh: 这次和上次发生的情况。理解你的改动产生了什么影响。

cues.en: And all of this data is being collected and stored because today digital storage is free. And so your entire history of what you've done with this project automatically becomes a kind of notebook
cues.zh: 所有这些数据都会被收集和存储，因为如今数字存储是免费的。于是，你在这个项目里做过的全部历史，就自动变成了一本笔记本

cues.en: where you can just browse through everything you've done. You can see all the video. You can see all the data. You can see any notes you took. And you can search. So if you notice that a sensor reading is kind of high,
cues.zh: 你可以随意浏览自己做过的一切。你能看到所有视频，所有数据，以及你记过的任何笔记。还能搜索。所以如果你发现某个传感器读数有点高，

cues.en: you wonder, like, was it ever that high in the past? You just search for that. You find sessions in the past that meet that condition. You just go in there and you figure out what was going on.
cues.zh: 你会想，它过去有那么高过吗？直接搜一下。你会找到过去满足这个条件的会话。进去看看，就能弄清楚当时发生了什么。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: the most critical thing here is that all this is just... Is taken for granted. Right? It's just built into the material. It's built into the room. The maker doesn't have to think of... Think about it. They don't need to, like, do anything special. They just show up and start building stuff. And all these tools are just at their disposal.
cues.zh: 这里最关键的是，这一切都只是……被视为理所当然。对吧？它已经内置在材料里。内置在房间里。创客不用去想着……去考虑它。他们不需要做什么特别的事。只要到场，开始搭建东西就行。而且所有这些工具都任他们使用。

cues.en: So once you're able to see across time, now there's an even more powerful way of seeing, which is seeing across different design alternatives.
cues.zh: 所以，一旦你能跨时间查看，现在还有一种更强大的查看方式，就是跨不同设计方案来查看。

cues.en: So should we make the robot behave like this or behave like that? Well, you do it both ways and you see which one works.
cues.zh: 那么，我们应该让机器人这样表现，还是那样表现？那就两种都做一遍，看看哪种可行。

cues.en: If you have a robot that's supposed to go towards the light, you might need to give it a setting to say, like, how sensitive it should be to the light. And the way that's done today is often with a kind of knob where you try it out in the setting. Oh, that don't work too well, so we try it out in this setting. Maybe that works better. You're kind of poking around. It's very ad hoc, very unsystematic.
cues.zh: 如果你有一个机器人， supposed to朝光走，你可能需要给它一个设置，比如它对光的敏感度应该是多少。而如今的做法通常是用一种旋钮，你在某个设置下试一下。哦，效果不太好，那我们在这个设置下试试。也许那个效果更好。你就是在到处摸索。这非常随意，非常不系统。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: I'm talking about an environment where instead of choosing one particular setting,
cues.zh: 我说的是一种环境，在这里不是选择某一个特定设置，

cues.en: you can just go across an entire range
cues.zh: 而是可以直接遍历整个范围

cues.en: and you just say go.
cues.zh: 你只需说开始。

cues.en: And the room and the material work together to do a test run at that setting, Try it out. Collect that data.
cues.zh: 房间和材料协同工作，在该设置下进行一次测试运行，试一试。收集数据。

cues.en: And then automatically try the next one.
cues.zh: 然后自动尝试下一个。

cues.en: And try the next one. Go through that entire range. Try them all out. Collect all the data.
cues.zh: 再试下一个。遍历整个范围。把它们都试一遍。收集所有数据。

cues.en: And then you can just look at it and see what actually happened in all those cases. You have all the data. You can take measurements.
cues.zh: 然后你就可以直接查看，看看在所有这些情况下实际发生了什么。你拥有全部数据。你可以进行测量。

cues.en: You can reduce the data. You can figure out which is the actual best possibility.
cues.zh: 你可以精简数据。你可以找出哪个才是真正的最佳可能性。

cues.en: And not just which one is the best, but why it's the best. You can see all the context.
cues.zh: 不只是哪个最好，而是为什么它最好。你能看到所有上下文。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: designing this kind of seeing space
cues.zh: 设计这种观察空间

cues.en: where the entire focus is being able to see and understand what this complex thing you're building is actually doing.
cues.zh: 其全部重点在于能够看到并理解你所构建的这个复杂事物实际上在做什么。

cues.en: Shifting the emphasis from putting material together to seeing and understanding in powerful ways.
cues.zh: 把重点从组合材料转移到以强大的方式观察和理解。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: And

cues.en: some of what I'm talking about is probably
cues.zh: 我要讲的一些内容可能

cues.en: gonna be expensive,
cues.zh: 会挺费钱的，

cues.en: but that's the entire point of a maker space is shared access to expensive tools.
cues.zh: 但这正是创客空间的意义所在——共享使用昂贵的工具。

cues.en: That's the reason to think of this as a a shared space.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么应该把它看作一个共享空间。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: some of this might be a bit of an engineering challenge to build,
cues.zh: 其中一些东西在工程上可能有点挑战性，

cues.en: but,
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: three d printers and space shuttles are also engineering challenges.
cues.zh: 3D打印机和航天飞机同样也是工程挑战。

cues.en: And we as a culture have decided those are important things that we want to have.
cues.zh: 而我们作为一种文化，已经认定这些是我们想要拥有的重要事物。

cues.en: And so really kind of the main thing that's needed here is the recognition of how important seeing is
cues.zh: 所以这里真正需要的主要是对“看见”有多重要的认识

cues.en: and the will to do something about it.
cues.zh: 以及为此付诸行动的意愿。

cues.en: I wanna I wanna close by
cues.zh: 我想在最后

cues.en: explaining why I feel this is so important.
cues.zh: 解释一下为什么我觉得这如此重要。

cues.en: We talk a lot about making nowadays,
cues.zh: 如今我们经常谈论创客，

cues.en: but the way I see it is making exists on a spectrum.
cues.zh: 但在我看来，创客是存在于一个谱系上的。

cues.en: There's these different ways of thinking that we draw on in different combinations at different times.
cues.zh: 有不同的思维方式，我们在不同时间以不同组合来运用它们。

cues.en: So on the left, I've put tinkering,
cues.zh: 所以在左边，我放了“捣鼓”，

cues.en: which is where you're trying stuff out, you're trying to find something that works, and you don't really understand the underlying principles by which it works. You don't really have a clear mental model for why this works and that doesn't, but you find something that works and you go with it. And this is a very important way of thinking,
cues.zh: 也就是你在尝试各种东西，试图找到能用的方案，但你并不真正理解它运作的底层原理。你并没有清晰的心智模型来解释为什么这个行那个不行，但你找到了能用的东西就用了。这是一种非常重要的思维方式，

cues.en: especially for beginners. This is where we all have to start.
cues.zh: 尤其对初学者来说。我们都是从这里开始的。

cues.en: But it's also important that on the spectrum it kind of fades over into engineering,
cues.zh: 但同样重要的是，在谱系上它逐渐过渡到工程，

cues.en: which is where you do understand the underlying principles.
cues.zh: 也就是你确实理解底层原理的地方。

cues.en: You do have a clear model of why this thing works. It's often a mathematical model. You can write a few equations that describes how the thing behaves.
cues.zh: 你对这件事为什么有效有清晰的模型。通常是数学模型，你能写出几个方程来描述它的行为。

cues.en: So you have this theoretical knowledge that's guiding your design decisions, and that's incredibly powerful.
cues.zh: 所以你有这种理论知识来指导设计决策，这非常强大。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但

cues.en: what do you do,
cues.zh: 当你没有这种理论知识时，

cues.en: when you don't have that theoretical knowledge? So this theoretical knowledge often comes from something like a textbook. What about when you're working in a domain where the textbooks haven't been written yet? And that's when we start moving over to the right side towards more scientific way of thinking,
cues.zh: 你该怎么办？这种理论知识通常来自教科书之类的东西。如果你在一个教科书还没被写出来的领域工作呢？这时我们就开始向右移动，转向更科学的思维方式，

cues.en: where you're discovering and codifying
cues.zh: 去发现并编纂

cues.en: those underlying principles, where you're generating that theory that engineering relies on.
cues.zh: 那些底层原理，去生成工程所依赖的理论。

cues.en: And this is incredibly powerful because this is how we explore and map out new territory.
cues.zh: 这非常强大，因为这就是我们探索和绘制新领域的方式。

cues.en: This is how you build new kinds of things and understand them deeply enough to build them reliably and robustly.
cues.zh: 这就是你构建新类型事物、并深入理解到足以可靠且稳健地构建它们的方式。

cues.en: So where all this fits in with tools is if you just give somebody construction tools and teach them how to use it,
cues.zh: 那么这一切和工具的关系是：如果你只给某人施工工具并教他们怎么用，

cues.en: they can work in this range.
cues.zh: 他们能在这个范围内工作。

cues.en: If you then also give somebody conceptual tools, if you give them theory,
cues.zh: 如果你再给某人概念工具，给他们理论，

cues.en: now they can work across this range.
cues.zh: 现在他们就能跨越这个范围工作。

cues.en: But if you want somebody to span that entire space, to be able to draw on all those ways of thinking,
cues.zh: 但如果你想让某人覆盖整个空间，能调用所有这些思维方式，

cues.en: they need to be able to see what they're doing. They need powerful seeing tools so they can see what's going on and understand it really deeply.
cues.zh: 他们需要能看见自己在做什么。他们需要强大的“看见”工具，才能看清发生了什么并真正深入地理解它。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: that's
cues.zh: 这就是

cues.en: the real reason why I'm interested in building a space like this, is because I think people need to work in a space that moves them away from the kinds of non scientific thinking that you do when you can't see what you're doing.
cues.zh: 我之所以有兴趣构建这样一个空间的真正原因，是因为我认为人们需要在一个能让他们摆脱非科学思维的空间里工作——那种在你无法看清自己在做什么时才会有的思维方式。

cues.en: Moves them away from blindly following recipes,
cues.zh: 让他们摆脱盲目照搬配方，

cues.en: from superstitions and rules of thumb,
cues.zh: 摆脱迷信和经验法则，

cues.en: and moves them towards
cues.zh: 引导他们走向

cues.en: deeply understanding what they're doing,
cues.zh: 深入理解自己在做什么，

cues.en: inventing new things, discovering new things, contributing back to the global pool of human knowledge.
cues.zh: 发明新事物、发现新事物，回馈全球人类知识库。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
